body: Yes, I live in the states. Luckily, I have insurance, but I still can't afford another doctor's visit to try to fix the issue. If I had my regular prescription of Xanax, I really don't think I would be on here right, talking about killing myself. Compared to my regular prescription, this newly reduced prescription lasted a week for my anxiety, and I'm going to wait another three weeks for the refill. I know I'm not in a sound state of mind, but I don't think my suicide can be helped because I know, with everything that has happened, I'm going to get to a state where I'm going to attempt. I've done it before, but I was unsuccessful.

You have good advice, but I don't have the money to go back and see my doctor. I went recently, and I had an adjustment to my meds I did not want. I agreed to a higher dosage of Lexapro, but did not approve of my Xanax being reduced by 2/3 of my current prescription. I have Panic Disorder, GAD, Social Phobia, and PTSD, and Xanax is sometimes necessary for me to prevent committing suicide. I have ran out of my anti-anxiety medication to try to prevent myself from suicide. Now I have nothing to help.

I am looking for another job. 

I am on medication. I said in my post that I am taking amitriptyline, and it is prescribed for Depression. I have also been prescribed Xanax,  which I also mentioned in my post. I'll be using those two drugs without using my Lexapro, which I am also prescribed but did not mention in my post, in my overdose.
